subject: Mutual Action Plan: unit-cost sanity checks + close timeline
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@helixmed.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <s.patel@helixmed.com>, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost details we need

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the call earlier. For the MAP we need a very short, defensible unit-econ summary to include in our procurement package. Specifically: tokens per API call assumptions for our 3 primary flows (patient intake, triage chat, summarization), expected batching impact at 95th pct latency target, and any KV/prefix caching assumptions that materially change monthly spend.

Can you share a simple sensitivity table (tokens/$ at low/nominal/high traffic), and a recommended acceptance threshold we can bake into the MAP? Procurement also asked for sample prompts so they can size expected token counts.

Appreciate it,
Anita
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@helixmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost details we need

Anita — thanks, sending a concise pack below and attaching a sensitivity workbook. High level first:

- Baseline model: m-llama-13B-quant (validated with your sample prompt set).
- Nominal tokens per flow (prompt + expected response):
  • Patient intake form: 220 tokens
  • Triage chat (avg turn): 380 tokens
  • Visit summarization (long): 4,200 tokens (often streamed)
- Assumptions that change tokens/$ by >20%:
  • Disabled prefix caching on triage = +18% token usage
  • Reducing batch size to prioritize <150ms P95 adds ~12% per-token overhead
  • Switching to smaller model variant (m-llama-7B) reduces cost/unit by ~28% but increases summary error rate (we flagged quality regression in evals)

I attached unit_econ_sensitivity.xlsx with a tokens-per-dollar sheet and a per-flow sensitivity slider. Quick recommendation for the MAP: require a nominal tokens/$ baseline and a 10% contingency buffer on top of expected spend for the pilot stage. That gives procurement headroom for bursty triage traffic and avoids premature cutoffs.

Im copying Ben for batching/caching implementation notes and Karthik for queueing/latency guardrails.

—Neha

Attachments: unit_econ_sensitivity.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@helixmed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost details we need

Anita - a couple of operational clarifications to make the numbers actionable:

- Batching: our runtime groups requests based on compatible model & max_seq. For triage, if you keep the average turn length under ~600 tokens we can achieve a steady-state batching factor of ~4 on your traffic shape (saves ~35% on GPU token cost). If you spike long context (summaries) batching drops and cost delta tightens.

- Prefix/KV caching: caching common patient intake prefixes (e.g., structured intake template) reduces prompt-side tokens by ~45% for that flow; enable at MAP start. For triage, caching helps when follow-ups reuse the same patient context (saves ~12% typical).

- Latency SLO impact: to hit P95 <200ms for triage we recommend configuring max_batch_latency=6ms and target batch_size <=6 for warm pools; that guidance is already encoded in the attached workbook scenario 'P95-200ms'.

Operational ask for MAP: add two acceptance gates — (1) sample_prompts.jsonl validated against eval harness (quality and tokens within +/-15% of expected), (2) pilot spend delta < +20% vs modeled baseline in first two weeks or trigger rollback.

Ben
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@helixmed.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <s.patel@helixmed.com>, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost details we need

Thanks — this is helpful. A few quick follow-ups before we finalize the MAP milestones:

1) Can you convert that sensitivity workbook to a single page summary (tokens/$ at 5th/50th/95th percentile) we can include in procurement packet?
2) For the acceptance gate on prompt validation, who runs the eval harness? We will need the results as a PDF or a drive link.
3) If we pick the 10% contingency buffer, what does a conservative two-week overage look like in absolute dollars for our expected pilot of 50k triage turns and 1k summaries?

If you can get those by EOD tomorrow well include them in the legal/finance review.

—Anita
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@helixmed.com>, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost details we need

Anita — attaching the one-pager (see Drive link) and a conservative two-week overage calc pasted below. Also included: instructions to run the eval harness (we can run it and drop a PDF) and the sample_prompt_set.jsonl you asked for.

Two-week conservative overage (10% buffer applied to modeled baseline):
- Modeled baseline monthly:
  • Triage (50k turns): 50,000 turns * 380 tokens/turn = 19,000,000 tokens
  • Summaries (1k): 1,000 * 4,200 = 4,200,000 tokens
  • Total tokens = 23,200,000 tokens
- Baseline tokens/$ (nominal sheet): 1,000,000 tokens = $55 (m-llama-13B-quant estimate) => tokens/$ = 18,181 tokens per $1
- Baseline spend = 23,200,000 / 18,181 = ~$1,277
- 10% buffer = +$128 => two-week overage window (assuming pilot is two-week slice ~50% of monthly) => ~$64 expected additional charge during the two-week pilot window above modeled pilot spend.

Notes: the workbook has alternate rows for different model choices; switching to m-llama-7B pushes tokens/$ to ~25,000 tokens per $1 but we flagged a quality drop for summarization in our evals.

Next steps for MAP doc: Ill produce the one-page percentiles PDF and run the eval harness on your sample_prompts.jsonl tomorrow morning; will upload results to the Drive link and share the HubSpot record.

Neha

Attachments uploaded: sample_prompt_set.jsonl
Drive link: https://drive.company.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helixmed-eval
